subject: PrivDeploy: volume-triggered discount cadence & incident-credit mechanics
messages:
From: Amelia Hart <amelia@helixcare.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helixcare.com
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Commercial ask — private deployment credits and SLA language

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to surface two things before we move the SOW to legal:

1) We need a clear cadence for volume-triggered discounts on the Private (VPC) package. HelixCare expects a pilot month with low usage followed by ramp. We want discounts to kick in automatically at pre-agreed monthly token thresholds rather than renegotiating each quarter.

2) Incident credits for Sev1/Sev2 events: instead of only an availability SLA credit, can Redwood provide an operational incident credit that offsets the platform fee when your incidents materially affect production? The ops team prefers credits that apply to the next invoice rather than one-off goodwill.

I've attached our draft SOW and a one-page SOC2 summary for context. Can you share an example cadence and a sample credit calculation we could include in the SOW?

Best,
Amelia Hart
Head of Cloud Ops, HelixCare
Attachment: Helix_SOW_draft_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Hart <amelia@helixcare.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2026 09:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Commercial ask — private deployment credits and SLA language

Amelia —

Appreciate the clear ask — this is manageable, and we've successfully modeled similar constructs for other PrivDeploy customers. High-level response below, then I'll drop a one-page example cadence for the SOW.

- Volume-triggered discounts: we can define tiered discounts that apply automatically once monthly consumption (measured in inference units/tokens and operator nodes) exceeds thresholds. Typical structure:
  * Month 1 (pilot): no discount, platform fee amortized over pilot only.
  * Months 2–6: ramp tiers with 5% at Tier A (>= X tokens), 10% at Tier B (>= Y tokens).
  * 12-month anchor: if annualized usage hits the committed floor, we apply a retroactive true-up credit.

We can keep the thresholds and percentages configurable in the SOW; will propose two banding options (conservative and aggressive) in the attachment.

- Incident credits: Redwood can offer incident credits that apply to the platform fee portion of the next invoice. Mechanics we propose: credits are expressed as a percentage of the monthly platform fee tied to severity and SLA miss duration. Example: 10% credit for cumulative Sev2 impact > 4 hours in a billing month; 25% credit for any Sev1 > 30 minutes after remediation SLA window. Credits are capped at a percentage of that month's platform fee (suggest cap at 50%) to avoid open-ended exposure.

I'll note two internal constraints for transparency: finance requires a maximum annual credit exposure (we can quantify in the SOW) and legal will want clear definitions of severity and blackout periods.

I'll attach a one-page cadence and a sample credit table. If that looks good, Irene and Marissa can help finalize language for the SOW.

Next steps: I will attach the sample cadence by EOD. Does HelixCare prefer credits applied only to platform fee (recommended) or to both platform fee + support retainer?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Principal Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-discount-cadence.pdf (pdf stub)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Amelia Hart <amelia@helixcare.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Commercial ask — private deployment credits and SLA language

Thanks Jordan — copying in high level legal guardrails so the SOW language is actionable:

1) Definitions: we need to codify what constitutes Sev1 and Sev2, the measurement windows, and what counts as customer-impacting (vs scheduled maintenance or customer's misconfiguration). Suggested clause: incidents must be logged in Redwood's incident tracker, validated by both parties within 72 hours, and then creditable.

2) Credit mechanics: credits applied to the next invoice are acceptable. For pilot customers we prefer a 12-month lookback for any retroactive true-up (to ensure usage is stable).

3) Platform fee amortization: we can offer to amortize the platform fee over the committed horizon if HelixCare takes a 12-month minimum commitment. Without the commit, we keep platform fee monthly with smaller upfront discounts.

4) Escalation: include a named escalation path (two contacts on both sides) and a one-week remediation cadence before additional contract remedies.

Marissa — please chime on finance exposure and what level of cap we should propose in the SOW.

Irene Choi
Head of Solutions & Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SLA-Rollup.docx (docx)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Amelia Hart <amelia@helixcare.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Commercial ask — private deployment credits and SLA language

Amelia / team — quick finance perspective:

- We can accept incident credits applied against the next invoice. For commercial protection, we propose:
  * A rolling 12-month maximum credit exposure equal to 25% of annualized platform fees (this protects Redwood from repeated high-frequency credits).
  * Pilot months are excluded from the rolling lookback for true-up; credits during pilot will be handled case-by-case.

- On the discount cadence: retroactive true-up credits (when annualized usage exceeds the committed floor) should be limited to a one-time annual reconciliation payment. In other words, we will apply a retroactive credit once per 12-month period rather than every month.

If HelixCare wants monthly automatic discounting without a committed anchor, the discount rates need to be smaller (we can do 3%/6% bands). If you commit 12 months at a minimum spend, we can open to the 5%/10% banding Jordan suggested and a higher true-up cap.

Happy to model the two scenarios if you can confirm expected token ranges for months 2–6.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
VP, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Amelia Hart <amelia@helixcare.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Commercial ask — private deployment credits and SLA language

Team — thanks, that framing is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- We are willing to commit to a 12-month minimum but need a sensible entry floor. For months 2–6 we expect token usage in the 1.5–2x pilot baseline, with potential to double by month 9. I'll confirm approximate token numbers by EOD Tuesday.

- HelixCare prefers incident credits apply to platform fee only; support retainer should remain separate. The rolling 12-month cap of 25% sounds acceptable as long as there is a clear definition of what counts toward the cap (you've defined it as annualized platform fees — ok).

- We can accept a single annual true-up for retroactive usage credits. For operational clarity, please include the one-sheet cadence and the exact sample math (how a 10% credit is calculated) in the SOW appendix.

Next steps: I'll send the month-by-month expected usage numbers and confirm the procurement contact for signature.

Best,
Amelia Hart
Head of Cloud Ops, HelixCare
Attachment: SOC2_Summary.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Hart <amelia@helixcare.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Commercial ask — private deployment credits and SLA language

Perfect — thanks Amelia. I will:

1) Produce the one-page discount cadence with two banding options (conservative / aggressive) and include sample math for the 10%/25% credits applied to the monthly platform fee.
2) Draft SOW appendix language that captures definitions (Sev1/Sev2), incident validation windows, credit caps, and the annual true-up mechanics.
3) ETA: draft appendix + cadence by EOD Thursday, internal review with Irene/Marissa on Friday, then I will circulate a SOW ready for HelixCare procurement signature next week.

If procurement can share expected token ranges tomorrow, that will speed the modeling.

Jordan Blake
Principal Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Bcc: internal notes (finance model ready once ranges received)
